statements.status_notes: Debian fixed this for trixie in libevent 2.1.13-stable-1~deb13u1 (DSA-6493-1), which ships the upstream 2.1.13-stable point release, and the DHI build of that Debian version carries the fix. Upstream commit https://github.com/libevent/libevent/commit/ef38f926e9cd1f082416c6fff13587bc1f431d72 stores the connection address in a sockaddr_storage and checks the address length unconditionally, so it no longer depends on an assertion that NDEBUG builds remove. Checked by inspecting the DHI Debian packages on amd64 and arm64 with their debug symbols. bufferevent_socket_set_conn_address_ in the libevent-2.1 and libevent-core-2.1 shared libraries and in the libevent.a and libevent_core.a static archives compares the length with 128 bytes and returns an error when it is larger; in builds without the fix it compares with 28 bytes and only asserts. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-63388 and https://github.com/libevent/libevent/security/advisories/GHSA-cvq5-vrvr-j338.
